content: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a widespread virus that has the potential to cause various types of cancer. HPV is directly linked to several cancers, including cervical cancer and oropharyngeal cancer, which affects the back of the throat. In addition to cancer, HPV can also lead to the development of warts. Preventative measures, such as the HPV vaccine and regular cervical cancer screenings, are effective in reducing the risk of cancers associated with HPV. Each year in the United States, approximately 37,000 cases of cancer are attributed to HPV infections. Among these, cervical cancer tends to be diagnosed at younger ages compared to other cancers caused by HPV. Many cancers associated with HPV are preventable. According to Dr. Virginia Senkomago from the CDC, recent data highlights the significant potential for prevention of these cancers through vaccination and early detection. As explained by pediatrician Dr. Jose Rodriguez, some HPV infections can lead to cancers such as cervical cancer or cancer in the back of the throat.
